questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: A car travelling at 20 m/s brakes with uniform deceleration and comes to rest in a distance of 50 m.
learning_objectives: K1 Use the equations of uniformly accelerated motion
F3 Explain motion using Newton's first law

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the magnitude of the deceleration of the car.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the time taken for the car to stop.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the braking distance would be larger on a wet road.

marking.final_answer: (a) 4.0 m/s² (b) 5.0 s (c) less friction, so smaller decelerating force
marking.worked_solution: (a) v² = u² − 2as ⇒ a = u²/(2s) = 400/100 = 4.0 m/s². (b) t = u/a = 20/4.0 = 5.0 s. (c) Wet road reduces friction between tyres and road, so the maximum decelerating force and deceleration are smaller; the car travels further.

points.description: Less friction / grip on wet road
So smaller deceleration and greater distance

evidence.quote: A car travelling at 20 m/s brakes with uniform deceleration and comes to rest in a distance of 50 m.

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: A ball of mass 0.50 kg is dropped from rest from a height of 3.2 m. Air resistance is negligible. Take g = 9.8 m/s².
learning_objectives: E1 Calculate gravitational potential and kinetic energy

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the gravitational potential energy lost by the ball as it falls to the ground.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the speed of the ball just before it hits the ground.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how the speed just before impact would change if air resistance were not negligible.

marking.final_answer: (a) 15.7 J (b) 7.9 m/s (c) lower speed: some energy transferred to the surroundings
marking.worked_solution: (a) ΔEp = mgh = 0.50 × 9.8 × 3.2 = 15.68 ≈ 15.7 J. (b) ½mv² = mgh ⇒ v = √(2gh) = √62.72 = 7.9 m/s. (c) Work done against air resistance transfers energy to the surroundings, so less kinetic energy and a lower speed.

points.description: Equates kinetic energy gained to potential energy lost
Less kinetic energy so lower speed

evidence.quote: A ball of mass 0.50 kg is dropped from rest from a height of 3.2 m. Air resistance is negligible. Take g = 9.8 m/s².

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: The table shows the velocity of a sprinter at different times after the start of a race.
learning_objectives: K2 Interpret motion data in tables and graphs
K1 Use the equations of uniformly accelerated motion

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the acceleration of the sprinter during the first 4.0 s.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the distance travelled in the first 6.0 s.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe the motion of the sprinter between 4.0 s and 6.0 s.

marking.final_answer: (a) 1.5 m/s² (b) 24 m (c) constant velocity of 6.0 m/s
marking.worked_solution: (a) a = 6.0/4.0 = 1.5 m/s². (b) Distance = ½ × 4.0 × 6.0 + 6.0 × 2.0 = 12 + 12 = 24 m. (c) Constant velocity (zero acceleration).

evidence.quote: The table shows the velocity of a sprinter at different times after the start of a race.

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: An electric kettle is connected to a 230 V mains supply and draws a current of 8.0 A.

marking.final_answer: (a) 1840 W (b) 2.2 × 10^5 J (c) larger current; thicker cable has lower resistance so less heating
marking.worked_solution: (a) P = VI = 230 × 8.0 = 1840 W. (b) E = Pt = 1840 × 120 = 220 800 J ≈ 2.2 × 10⁵ J. (c) Large current; thick cable has lower resistance so it does not overheat.

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: A lift of total mass 900 kg accelerates upwards at 1.5 m/s². Take g = 9.8 m/s².
learning_objectives: F1 Apply Newton's second law F = ma
F3 Explain motion using Newton's first law

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the weight of the lift.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the tension in the lift cable.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the tension is smaller when the lift moves upwards at constant speed.

marking.final_answer: (a) 8820 N (b) 1.0 × 10^4 N (10 170 N) (c) at constant speed the resultant force is zero, so tension equals weight
marking.worked_solution: (a) W = mg = 900 × 9.8 = 8820 N. (b) T − mg = ma ⇒ T = m(g + a) = 900 × 11.3 = 10 170 N. (c) Constant speed ⇒ zero acceleration ⇒ zero resultant force ⇒ T = W = 8820 N, which is smaller.

points.description: So tension equals weight, smaller than before

evidence.quote: A lift of total mass 900 kg accelerates upwards at 1.5 m/s². Take g = 9.8 m/s².

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: Light travels from air into a glass block of refractive index 1.5. The speed of light in air is 3.0 × 10^8 m/s.
learning_objectives: W2 Describe and calculate refraction of light
W1 Use the wave equation v = f λ

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the speed of light in the glass.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a ray entering the glass at an angle changes direction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State what happens to the frequency of the light as it enters the glass, and give a reason.

marking.final_answer: (a) 2.0 × 10^8 m/s (b) speed decreases on entering the denser medium (c) unchanged; set by the source
marking.worked_solution: (a) v = c/n = 3.0 × 10⁸/1.5 = 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s. (b) The light slows down; one side of the wavefront slows first so the direction changes. (c) Frequency unchanged: it is determined by the source.

points.description: Wavefront slows unevenly, so direction changes

evidence.quote: Light travels from air into a glass block of refractive index 1.5. The speed of light in air is 3.0 × 10^8 m/s.
